commerceSaltTithes.name: Salt Tithes
commerceSaltTithes.flavor: Salt is weighed twice: once for the pot, once for the ledger.
commerceSaltTithes.text: Gain +3 gold per distinct accessible improved luxury you produce. Worked luxury tiles gain +1 food.

theGuildHalls.name: The Guild Halls
theGuildHalls.flavor: A craft is a secret kept in public.
theGuildHalls.text: A city gains +1 production per distinct luxury type it works. Worked camps and plantations gain +1 food.

theMerchantShrines.name: The Merchant Shrines
theMerchantShrines.flavor: Every scale has a god leaning on it.
theMerchantShrines.text: Your capital gains +2 faith. Cities working an improved luxury gain +2 faith, once per city.

travellersLetters.name: Travellers' Letters
travellersLetters.flavor: News travels with the cargo, and is worth more.
travellersLetters.text: Your capital gains +2 science and +2 culture, plus +1 of each per foreign empire met, at most +4 additional science and culture.
deferred: your capital learns and sings a little more for every foreign empire you have met
travellersLetters.note: Half built, and so held whole. Nothing in this game counts the empires you have met, so the letters have nobody to be addressed to.

lettersOfIntroduction.name: Letters of Introduction
lettersOfIntroduction.flavor: A stranger with a letter is not a stranger.
lettersOfIntroduction.text: First contact with each foreign empire grants you 100 gold and that empire 15 gold. Contact recorded before activation cannot pay retrospectively. Discoveries yield 15 gold.
deferred: meeting an empire for the first time pays you, and pays them
claiming a discovery pays gold
lettersOfIntroduction.note: Held whole. The world does not announce a first meeting, and no law of yours can put coin in another realm's treasury.

thePathfindersCompany.name: The Pathfinders' Company
thePathfindersCompany.flavor: Pay the man who knows where the water is.

theLighthouseKeepers.name: The Lighthouse Keepers
theLighthouseKeepers.flavor: A fire on a headland is the cheapest harbour there is.
theLighthouseKeepers.text: Ships gain +1 sight. Lighthouses cost 25% less production; worked fishing boats gain +1 food.

commerceTheAssayersRule.name: The Assayer's Rule
commerceTheAssayersRule.flavor: Every seam weighed, and weighed again.
commerceTheAssayersRule.text: Worked resource tiles that supply gold gain +1 gold.

theMineralTrade.name: The Mineral Trade
theMineralTrade.flavor: Ore that leaves the valley is worth more than ore that stays in it.
theMineralTrade.text: Worked mines and quarries gain +2 gold but lose 1 production.

coastalEstates.name: Coastal Estates
coastalEstates.flavor: The house looks at the water, and the water pays the house.
coastalEstates.text: Worked plantations and fishing boats gain +1 food and +1 gold.

landSpeculation.name: Land Speculation
landSpeculation.flavor: Buy the field before anyone knows what it is for.
landSpeculation.text: Buying tiles costs 50% less. Your capital loses 2 happiness.

foundingCapital.name: Founding Capital
foundingCapital.flavor: Somebody has to pay for the first roof, and it is never the settler.

privatePatronage.name: Private Patronage
privatePatronage.flavor: The purse builds faster than the quarry, and asks for its name on the door.
privatePatronage.text: Gold purchases of ordinary buildings cost 20% less. Producing those buildings normally takes 20% more production. Empire buildings and wonders are unaffected.
deferred: buying an ordinary building costs less, and raising one the slow way costs more
privatePatronage.note: Held whole. The realm's single great houses can be named now, and a marvel always could — but neither can be named by its absence, and this card is a discount on every building that is neither, so a discount written here would reach the great houses the card says it must not.

civicReceipts.name: Civic Receipts
civicReceipts.flavor: The town remembers who paid for the roof.
civicReceipts.text: Purchasing an ordinary building for the first time in a city grants culture equal to 10% of the gold paid, with no cap.
civicReceipts.note: The ledger of firsts is kept per town and marks the first building a town buys, whatever it was; the card then asks whether that building was one of the realm's single great houses and pays nothing if it was. A town that bought a great house before it bought anything else never collects.

provisioningContracts.name: Provisioning Contracts
provisioningContracts.flavor: Grain moves on paper long before it moves on a cart.
provisioningContracts.text: Domestic routes grant their destination +2 food and +2 production.

theCommonRoad.name: The Common Road
theCommonRoad.flavor: A road belongs to whoever is standing on it.
theCommonRoad.text: Your foreign routes grant you +2 gold, +2 science and +2 culture. Each also grants its host city +2 gold.
deferred: a road that ends abroad pays you, and pays the town it ends in
theCommonRoad.note: Half built, and so held whole. A law of yours pays your own books; it has no way to put coin in a foreign market.

theReturnLeg.name: The Return Leg
theReturnLeg.flavor: The cart comes back. Something should be in it.
theReturnLeg.text: Your domestic routes also pay their origin one third of the non-conversion food, production and gold they pay the destination. The destination loses nothing. Returned yields cannot circulate again.
deferred: a road pays the town it left as well as the town it reaches, and the second helping never travels again
theReturnLeg.note: Held whole. A caravan's earnings are banked where it arrives, and there is no way to send a share of them home.

ventureRoutes.name: Venture Routes
ventureRoutes.flavor: The far market pays for the risk of reaching it.
ventureRoutes.text: Your routes gain two turns of range. Routes whose endpoints are more than fourteen hexes apart gain +100% gold, using the shortest wrapped map distance.
deferred: your roads run longer before they lapse
a road between distant towns pays far more gold
ventureRoutes.note: Held whole. Nothing can lengthen a caravan's term, and a road's pay cannot be made to turn on how far it reaches.

theMerchantLedger.name: The Merchant Ledger
theMerchantLedger.flavor: A name written down is a name you can go back to.
theMerchantLedger.text: Hiring a new caravan costs 15% less. While active, gains +1 science and +1 culture per turn for each distinct destination city first reached by your routes, at most +24 of each.
deferred: hiring a caravan costs less
every new market your roads reach for the first time teaches and sings, for as long as you keep the ledger
theMerchantLedger.note: Held whole. No book in this game records which markets your caravans have already found.

theFactorsHouses.name: The Factors' Houses
theFactorsHouses.flavor: The factor never leaves. That is the whole of his value.
theFactorsHouses.text: Your cities holding your established commercial post gain +2 gold and +4 culture. Hiring a caravan from such a city costs 15% less.
deferred: the towns where your house is established pay gold and culture, and send caravans more cheaply
theFactorsHouses.note: Held whole. A standing commercial house is a new fact about a town, and nothing on the board keeps one yet.

thePlantersCharter.name: The Planters' Charter
thePlantersCharter.flavor: Break the ground first. The argument can follow.
thePlantersCharter.text: Once drafted, unlock the Plantation House for construction. No chair required. The building is purchased with gold; its payload is specified below.
deferred: drafting this opens the planters' house for building
thePlantersCharter.note: Held whole. The house it would open has not been drawn up yet, so the charter has nothing to grant.

boughtSwords.name: Bought Swords
boughtSwords.flavor: A hired sword is dearer to raise and cheaper to buy.
boughtSwords.text: Military units cost 20% less gold to purchase, but 10% more production to train. Purchases still do not count as training.

theConvoy.name: The Convoy
theConvoy.flavor: Guard the cart and you are guarding the year.
theConvoy.text: Your combat units within one hex of your trader gain +4 strength. Your traders gain +1 movement. Traders remain plunderable.
theConvoy.note: "Combat units" is the soldiers and the ships, which are two classes on the roster and so two lines here — the escort of a land road and the escort of a sea lane are the same promise made to both. A cart, a workman and a settler are none of them a combat unit and collect nothing.

theTreatyPorts.name: The Treaty Ports
theTreatyPorts.flavor: Two seals on one page, and the harbour opens.
theTreatyPorts.text: Each foreign empire with which you have an active resource agreement grants your capital +2 gold and +3 culture. That partner's capital gains +1 gold. Each partner counts once.
deferred: every partner you have a standing agreement with pays your capital, and theirs
theTreatyPorts.note: Held whole. Nothing counts your standing agreements, and no law of yours can pay a foreign capital.

thePostRiders.name: The Post Riders
thePostRiders.flavor: The road is only as good as the man who rides it at night.
thePostRiders.text: Your civilians and traders beginning a turn on a road you own gain +1 movement for that turn. Hiring and starting a route do not trigger another grant.
deferred: a cart or a workman that wakes on your own road travels further that turn
thePostRiders.note: Held whole. A piece can be paid for the ground it stands on, but the road under it is not among the grounds it can be asked about.

establishedRoutes.name: Established Routes
establishedRoutes.flavor: The second season is worth more than the first.
establishedRoutes.text: A trade route you have kept up for at least thirty turns pays 50% more. A route that lapses, is cancelled or is plundered begins its term again.

theMarketWrit.name: The Market Writ
theMarketWrit.flavor: Where the stalls stand, the writ runs.
theMarketWrit.text: +1 authority for every two Markets in your empire. Buying tiles costs 30% less.

commercialEducation.name: Commercial Education
commercialEducation.flavor: A boy who can keep a ledger can keep anything.

strategicReserves.name: Strategic Reserves
strategicReserves.flavor: Keep more than you need, and study what you keep.
strategicReserves.text: Worked strategic resource tiles gain +1 science and +1 gold.

marketFoundations.name: Market Foundations
marketFoundations.flavor: Lay the stones for the stalls, and the town arranges itself around them.
marketFoundations.text: Gain +20% production toward Markets. Markets provide +1 happiness.

financedIndustry.name: Financed Industry
financedIndustry.flavor: Coin buys the tools, and the men who used to eat go and use them.
financedIndustry.text: Cities gain production equal to 20% of their gold yield. Every city loses 3 food.
financedIndustry.note: The share is taken of the town's own flat coin as it stood before any conversion spoke, so a card that turns coin into hammers cannot feed a card that turns hammers into coin.

theHomeMarket.name: The Home Market
theHomeMarket.flavor: Every road that ends here was built for here.
theHomeMarket.text: Cities receiving at least two of your domestic routes gain +20% food, +20% production and +2 happiness, once per city.
deferred: a town that more than one of your own roads ends in grows, works and rests better
theHomeMarket.note: Held whole. A town can be asked whether a road ends in it, never how many do.

theCaravanseraiNetwork.name: The Caravanserai Network
theCaravanseraiNetwork.flavor: Spread the halts and the desert shrinks.
theCaravanseraiNetwork.text: Each city receiving a domestic trade route grants +1 happiness, once per city. Domestic routes gain +1 production and +1 gold.

theForeignFactor.name: The Foreign Factor
theForeignFactor.flavor: Our man in their market, and their man in ours.
theForeignFactor.text: Each foreign city holding your established commercial post grants you +3 gold and its host city +1 gold per turn while you are at peace and the host is not blockaded.
deferred: every foreign town where your house is established pays you, and pays its host, while the peace holds
theForeignFactor.note: Held whole. A standing commercial house abroad is a new fact about a town, and no law of yours can pay a foreign town.

theConsulate.name: The Consulate
theConsulate.flavor: A roof, a seal, and somebody who answers letters.
theConsulate.text: Cities holding your established commercial post purchase ordinary buildings and civilian units for 15% less gold, benefiting that city's owner. Each qualifying foreign host also grants you +2 culture while at peace and unblocked. Multiple foreign Consulates do not stack the discount.
deferred: towns where your house is established buy more cheaply, whoever owns them, and each foreign host sings for you
theConsulate.note: Held whole. A standing commercial house abroad has no place on the board, and a discount of yours cannot be handed to another empire.

theWarehouses.name: The Warehouses
theWarehouses.flavor: A full shed is an argument nobody wins.
theWarehouses.text: Each luxury type with at least four accessible improved deposits you produce grants +6 gold, +4 culture and +3 happiness. Exported copies still count for this card; imported and manufactured copies do not.
deferred: a luxury you dig in real quantity pays gold, culture and contentment
theWarehouses.note: Held whole. The realm can be asked which luxuries it holds more than one seam of, never which it holds a shed's worth of.

thePurpleWorks.name: The Purple Works
thePurpleWorks.flavor: The dye is worth more than the cloth, and the secret more than either.
thePurpleWorks.text: Once drafted, unlock the Purple Works for construction. No chair required. This national building supplies one manufactured luxury copy; its payload is specified below.
deferred: drafting this opens the purple works for building
thePurpleWorks.note: Held whole. The works it would open has not been drawn up yet, and neither has the good it would make.

theMoneyLenders.name: The Money Lenders
theMoneyLenders.flavor: Money left alone is the only servant that never sleeps.
theMoneyLenders.text: Earn interest equal to 2% of your treasury each turn, with no cap.
theMoneyLenders.note: The interest is a coin for every fiftieth in the treasury, which is the two per hundred the card quotes, counted off the bank as it stood when the books were opened and floored once.

theCharteredArsenal.name: The Chartered Arsenal
theCharteredArsenal.flavor: Pay on delivery, and inspect before you pay.
theCharteredArsenal.text: Military units purchased with gold gain +4 strength permanently on creation.

theHarbourChain.name: The Harbour Chain
theHarbourChain.flavor: Count the harbours and you have counted the fleet.
theHarbourChain.text: Gain +1 route capacity per two Harbours you own, at most +4. Sea routes gain +3 range and +1 gold for every 4 hexes travelled.
deferred: your harbours together open more roads than you could otherwise run
a road run by sea reaches further and pays by the distance it covers
theHarbourChain.note: Half built, and so held whole. Counting the harbours for extra roads is ordinary law now, and so is paying a road by its own length — but neither can be asked of a sea road alone, because nothing narrows a road's pay by the crossing it takes, and how far a road may reach is not a figure any law may move.

theLeagueOfCities.name: The League of Cities
theLeagueOfCities.flavor: The league is a promise between markets, not between kings.
theLeagueOfCities.text: Cities with one of your paying outgoing routes gain +15% production and cost one less authority, minimum one. Cities without one lose 10% gold.
deferred: a town that sends out one of your roads works harder and is easier to hold
a town that sends none loses gold
theLeagueOfCities.note: Held whole. A town can be asked whether a road ends in it, never whether one sets out from it, and no law makes a single town cheaper to hold.

theCharterFleet.name: The Charter Fleet
theCharterFleet.flavor: A hull bought is a hull at sea this season.
theCharterFleet.text: Naval combat units cost 20% less gold to purchase. Naval combat units you purchase with gold gain +1 movement permanently. Normal coastal, technology and purchase requirements remain.

exportGuilds.name: Export Guilds
exportGuilds.flavor: The province that sells abroad builds at home.
exportGuilds.text: A city working a luxury type you currently export through an active agreement gains +20% production toward ordinary buildings and +2 happiness, once per city.
deferred: a town working a good you are currently selling abroad builds faster and rests easier
exportGuilds.note: Held whole. Nothing asks whether a particular good is being sold abroad this turn.

theExchange.name: The Exchange
theExchange.flavor: Two ledgers open on one table is the oldest university there is.
theExchange.text: Each different foreign empire your routes currently serve grants you +5% science and culture empire wide. Each served empire's capital gains +2 science and +2 culture.
deferred: every foreign realm your roads reach teaches your whole empire, and learns from it
theExchange.note: Half built, and so held whole. A law of yours pays your own books; it cannot teach a foreign capital.

theBrokersRedraw.name: The Brokers' Redraw
theBrokersRedraw.flavor: Anything can be bought, including another look at the table.
theBrokersRedraw.text: You may reroll a draft with gold instead of faith. All other purchasing is 10% more expensive.
deferred: a hand may be redrawn for coin instead of for prayer, and everything else you buy costs more
theBrokersRedraw.note: A line the design is still writing, entered under a working name so that it is not lost. A redraw is paid for out of the faith bank and nothing else, and the bank a redraw draws on is not a thing a law may change.

theScholarsRoads.name: The Scholars' Roads
theScholarsRoads.text: Lose 4 route capacity. Your routes gain +2 science and +2 culture, and gain +50% science and culture.

theCustomsHouses.name: The Customs Houses
theCustomsHouses.flavor: The gate that counts you is the gate that knows you.
theCustomsHouses.text: Customs houses gain +3 gold and +1 renown. Cities with a customs house gain +15% gold toward purchasing.
deferred: a customs house pays gold and renown, and its town buys more with what it earns
theCustomsHouses.note: A line the design is still writing, entered under a working name so that it is not lost. Renown is paid for a town's buildings and never for one hex's works, and no town's gold can be made to go further at the counter.

civicMarkets.name: Civic Markets
civicMarkets.flavor: The stalls teach arithmetic to everybody who buys anything.

maritimeAuthority.name: Maritime Authority
maritimeAuthority.flavor: The flag over the harbour is the flag over the coast.
maritimeAuthority.text: Gain +3 authority. Naval units gain +5 combat strength against cities.

professionalRetainers.name: Professional Retainers
professionalRetainers.flavor: Men who are paid to fight fight better, and keep being paid.
professionalRetainers.text: All units gain +3 combat strength and cost +1 gold in maintenance.

theDyeVats.name: The Dye Vats
theDyeVats.flavor: The colour costs the town its coin and pays it back in song.
theDyeVats.text: Once drafted, unlock the Dye Vats for construction. No chair required. This purchased building turns its city's worked luxuries toward culture and faith; its payload is specified below.
deferred: drafting this opens the dye vats for building
theDyeVats.note: Held whole. The vats they would open have not been drawn up yet, so the charter has nothing to grant.

theEndowment.name: The Endowment
theEndowment.flavor: Buy the roof, and endow the men under it.
theEndowment.text: Ordinary buildings you purchase gain a permanent bonus to each positive native yield equal to 25% of that yield, with a minimum bonus of +2 per positive yield type. Replacing a building cannot stack the stamp.
deferred: a building you buy is better for the rest of its life than one you raised
theEndowment.note: Held whole. A building now remembers the turn it was raised, but not the bank that paid for it — a soldier can be marked at his birth by the till, and a building cannot, so nothing can tell a bought roof from a hammered one afterwards.

thePaidArmy.name: The Paid Army
thePaidArmy.flavor: An army that is paid on time is a cheap army.
thePaidArmy.text: Military-unit upkeep falls by 1 gold, minimum zero. Military units cost 25% less gold to purchase.

merchantPrinces.name: Merchant Princes
merchantPrinces.flavor: Genius is expensive, and the price is quoted.
merchantPrinces.text: Gold may purchase great-person drafts at the existing escalating offer price, with normal availability and purchase limits.

theWorldsExchange.name: The World's Exchange
theWorldsExchange.flavor: The last work of the age is paid for by every market in it.
theWorldsExchange.text: Each different foreign empire currently served by your routes grants +10% production toward the Opus, at most +40%. Existing construction and victory requirements remain.
theWorldsExchange.note: Held whole. Hammers behind a thing are raised by a flat share, never by a share counted off how far your roads reach.

theCharteredMetropolis.name: The Chartered Metropolis
theCharteredMetropolis.flavor: One city, and every road in the world leading to it.
theCharteredMetropolis.text: Cities with at least three of your paying outgoing routes gain +25% food, production and culture, but each costs +4 authority while qualified.
deferred: a town that sends out several of your roads grows and works and sings far better, and is far harder to hold
theCharteredMetropolis.note: Held whole. A town can be asked whether a road ends in it, never how many set out from it, and no law raises what one town costs to hold.

theAdmiraltyOfTrade.name: The Admiralty of Trade
theAdmiraltyOfTrade.flavor: The sea has no middle, only two ends.
theAdmiraltyOfTrade.text: Your sea routes may connect two cities holding your established commercial posts regardless of range. A legal sea path, access, peace and route capacity are still required.
deferred: a sea road between two of your established houses may be run at any distance
theAdmiraltyOfTrade.note: Held whole. A standing commercial house has no place on the board, and nothing may waive how far a road is allowed to reach.

theMerchantCommonwealth.name: The Merchant Commonwealth
theMerchantCommonwealth.flavor: Govern by ledger and the provinces govern themselves.
theMerchantCommonwealth.text: Each owned city with your established commercial post receiving a domestic route gains +2 happiness and costs one less authority, minimum one.
deferred: your own towns where your house is established and one of your roads ends rest easier and are easier to hold
theMerchantCommonwealth.note: Held whole. A standing commercial house has no place on the board, and no law makes a single town cheaper to hold.

theMerchantWorks.name: The Merchant Works
theMerchantWorks.flavor: Coin becomes stone, and stone outlasts the coin.
theMerchantWorks.text: Cities building an empire building, world wonder or the Opus gain production equal to 25% of their base city gold, but lose 20% of their gold income while doing so. Foreign-route empire gold and conversion outputs are excluded from the production basis.
deferred: a town raising one of the realm's great houses turns a share of its coin into stone, and loses a share of its coin while it does
theMerchantWorks.note: Half built, and so held whole. A town can be asked whether it is raising a wonder, but the realm's single great houses and the last work of all are not a class anything can name.

theGildedScaffold.name: The Gilded Scaffold
theGildedScaffold.flavor: Every marvel has a price. Most of them are simply not quoted.
theGildedScaffold.text: You may purchase world wonders. All your cities lose 15% production.
deferred: a wonder may be bought outright, and every town of yours works more slowly for it
theGildedScaffold.note: A line the design is still writing, entered under a working name so that it is not lost. A wonder is refused at the counter before a price is ever asked for, and nothing may open that door.
